_README: Expectations for scripts/db-tests/idor-sweep.mjs. A table appears here ONLY when its exposure is a
deliberate product decision, and the value is the reason. An empty or missing reason is not an entry.
publicRead    — signed-out visitors are meant to read this table (discovery, share links, SEO).
crossUserRead — a signed-in user is meant to see rows owned by someone else (public authorship,
counterparty visibility, admin review). Use 'table' or the narrower 'table.column'.
Adding an entry silences a finding, so each one is a claim you are making about the product.
Review this file whenever a policy changes.
Baselined 2026-09-20 against staging, with idor-fixtures.sql loaded. Everything listed below was
checked against what the product actually promises, not merely against what the database happened

publicRead.businesses: Shops are the catalogue. A signed-out visitor browsing the map is the primary funnel. read_businesses already narrows this to status=ACTIVE AND owner_enabled AND deleted_at IS NULL.
publicRead.providers: Same as businesses — independent providers are discoverable by design.
publicRead.catalog_items: Menu and price list of a public shop. Meaningless to hide when the shop itself is public.
publicRead.provider_packages: A provider's published service/price list, same reasoning as catalog_items.
publicRead.categories: Static taxonomy. No user data; the picker must work before sign-in.
publicRead.queue_settings: Whether a shop's queue is open and how long the wait is — the reason a guest opens the page.
publicRead.requests: Open 'asks' are public by design: the whole point is that nearby sellers can see and answer them. Guests must be able to read them to be persuaded to sign up.
publicRead.leaderboard_points: Deliberate public leaderboard (public_sel_leaderboard_points USING true). Columns are user_id, points, updated_at — no PII beyond a user id that public profiles already expose. CAVEAT: this does let an anonymous client enumerate every user id and activity level, which is a scraping vector rather than a leak. Revisit under the rate-limiting/anti-enumeration work, not as an RLS change.

crossUserRead.businesses: A shop is public; its owner_user_id is part of the public record.
crossUserRead.providers: As above — a provider profile is public.
crossUserRead.requests: Open asks are public, so reading another user's request is the product working.
crossUserRead.leaderboard_points: Public leaderboard; see the note in publicRead.
crossUserRead.bug_reports: Only admin1 reaches these, via is_admin(). Triage is impossible otherwise. Verified 2026-09-20: customer1 could NOT read customer2's rows.
crossUserRead.client_errors: Admin-only, same as bug_reports — this is the crash triage queue.
crossUserRead.support_tickets: Admin-only. Support staff must read the ticket they are answering.
crossUserRead.profile_deletion_requests: Admin-only. Deletion requests are reviewed by a human before the purge runs.
